fact: The Ministry of Health and Sanitation's HMIS procedures manual of April 2020 states that peripheral health units (CHCs, CHPs and MCHPs) compile monthly reports from paper registers onto standard HMIS summary forms and submit hard copies to the District Health Management Team by the fifth day after the month, where the district M&E officer verifies them and a data entry officer keys them into DHIS2; the national level receives the districts' data through DHIS2 by the fifteenth.

The April 2020 HMIS procedures manual states that in hospitals the hospital M&E officer receives hard copies from wards and units by the second day after the month and is responsible for entering the hospital's data into DHIS2 before the fifth day.

The April 2020 HMIS procedures manual has no peripheral health unit entering its own data: all report on paper to the district for entry, and the manual notes a plan for 2020, not then in effect, to decentralise electronic data entry into DHIS2 to the community health centres at chiefdom level, which would then take the other units' reports.

The April 2020 HMIS procedures manual states that hospitals enter their own monthly data into DHIS2 through a hospital M&E officer, while peripheral health units report on paper; it speaks of hospitals without separating district from tertiary and teaching hospitals.

The April 2020 HMIS procedures manual states that the Directorate of Policy, Planning and Information of the Ministry of Health and Sanitation is responsible for the routine health information system, its HMIS unit overseeing routine data collection and issuing DHIS2 user accounts, and that no partner may change HMIS tools or introduce parallel ones without the chief medical officer's approval.
